caveats: The defensible comparison window is January 1-June 30, 2018, not the entire 2018-2021 police award cycle.
The police-side observation is the Chief of Police, whom the ordinance explicitly identifies as removed from the police bargaining unit.
The non-safety side is an Administrative Assistant position rate, not a separately verified non-safety bargaining-unit contract record.
Role, rank, duties, work schedule, full-time status, and hours equivalence are not established.
The 199.2% figure is an arithmetic contrast between two documented position rates and must not be interpreted as an Alburtis bargaining-unit wage-gap estimate.
Manual/legal/substantive review is required before any analytic use beyond an appendix-level documentary illustration.
rows.why_usable_or_not: The exact values, hourly basis, regular/base character, and overlapping January-June 2018 period are source-grounded, and the arithmetic is correct. The comparison is usable only as a heavily qualified local documentary position-rate illustration because it does not satisfy the project's matched bargaining-unit unit of observation and lacks role/rank/hours comparability.

caveats: Ordinance 23-06 expressly labels the entries as maximum annual salaries and maximum hourly rates, not necessarily the employees' actual paid wages.
Section 2 states that the Mayor shall set each employee's actual salary and that it may be lower than the listed maximum.
The retained source is a December 12, 2023 council packet; the displayed ordinance copy has blank adoption and approval fields, so enactment should be confirmed before analytic use.

The comparison pairs a part-time patrol position with an administrative-assistant position and does not establish equivalence in duties, tenure, experience, hiring requirements, hours, or schedule placement.
The listed schedule excludes fringe benefits and citizen-donation amounts, so it is not a total-compensation comparison.
This is bounded local documentary evidence about authorized maximum hourly rates, not a final wage-gap estimate, nationally representative result, population-prevalence statement, or causal finding.
rows.why_usable_or_not: The two values are visually and textually confirmed on the same retained PDF page, in the same 2024 maximum salary schedule, with explicit hourly units, clear police and clerical/admin labels, and no conversion. The $5.00 and 25.0% calculations are correct. The evidence can therefore support a conditional PI-report example about a difference in listed maximum hourly rates. It cannot support an unqualified actual-wage differential because the ordinance says actual pay may be lower, the packet copy's enactment status is not established by the retained page, and the occupations are not substantively matched.

caveats: The police value is specifically the Year 1 entry step for officers hired after 1999, while the Code Enforcement Officer line provides a single listed rate with no tenure, step, or experience label.

The source establishes common municipality, cycle, page, hourly pay basis, and schedule-listed wage status, but it does not establish comparable tenure, experience, duties, qualifications, hours, full-time status, or schedule position.

The upstream normalized Code Enforcement Officer record was incorrectly tagged as police; this validation corrects the candidate interpretation from the verbatim source line but does not overwrite the raw upstream record.
The negative $0.91/hour documentary difference pertains only to these two specifically listed schedule values and must not be generalized to police and non-safety employees in Canastota.
This is bounded local documentary evidence, not a final wage-gap estimate, and is not nationally representative.
Substantive/manual validation of occupational and schedule-position comparability is required before analytic use beyond a qualified supporting example.
rows.why_usable_or_not: The values, hourly units, 2023-2024 cycle, municipal identity, safety/non-safety labels, source hashes, and arithmetic all validate directly against the same retained salary-schedule page. The candidate therefore supports a precisely bounded statement about two source-listed rates. It is not suitable for a main wage-gap finding because a Year 1 police step is not demonstrated to be substantively comparable to the single Code Enforcement Officer rate.

caveats: The comparison is between a group-wide part-time police rate and the rate for one part-time utility-clerk position.
The ordinance does not establish equivalence in duties, experience, schedule, or hiring requirements across the two occupations.
The utility-clerk line caps work at 28 hours; the police line does not state an hours cap on the same page.
The comparison is a bounded local documentary rate difference, not a final wage-gap estimate or a nationally representative result.
rows.why_usable_or_not: Both values are visually confirmed in the same operative 2024 municipal ordinance, both are explicit hourly base rates for part-time positions, the safety and non-safety classifications are clear, and no conversion is required. The source supports a bounded local documentary comparison, with occupational and work-schedule caveats.
